messages:
lia-support: FYI inbound: HealthMate is seeing a spike of 504s for hosted inference since ~12:07 UTC, all on the /v1/generate endpoint. Customer reports large prompts (30k+ tokens) timing out. example request_id=hc-7a2f5c.
alert-bot: [INCIDENT] High 504 rate detected on hosted-infer-prod (route: /v1/generate) — rate 18% p95 latency > 12s — alert -> #incidents.
mike-eng: looking at runner logs for that request_id now. early signs: worker container got SIGKILL and then restart. seeing GPU memory escalation then OOM kill. snippet: ```2026-03-17T12:07:28Z Runner[pid=4021]: Alloc attempt 14.8GB -> OOM; nvml reports out-of-memory; exit_code=137```
lia-support: customer says timeouts happen mid-response, sometimes partial output then cut. billing flag raised (they were charged for tokens but got 504). cs asked for ETA.
emma-reliability: can we confirm segfault vs OOM? exit_code=137 usually OOM; segfault would be signal 11. any coredump?
mike-eng: no core in the pod, but kube events show OOMKill. I also see a few recent containers that crashed with SIGSEGV on the same node (different pids within the minute). logs: ```signal 11 @ 0x7f2b1e... backtrace: attention_kernel+0x1234``` — could be mixed: memory OOM triggering unsafe kernel path then segfault.
sanjay-ml: workload detail: HealthMate calls with a long context + toolcall sequence that increases KV cache and forces large attention windows. Likely sequence-length growth -> KV cache map blowup. repro plan: send same long prompt with streaming enabled.
infra-oncall: mitigation: temporarily route this customer to dedicated fallback model (cpu-backed small model) while we stabilize. I've pinned HealthMate to fallback routing for now. also draining node gpu-node-72 to repro in a controlled fleet.
mike-eng: repro steps I used (local): 
1) run: ```curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -X POST https://api.redwood-hosted/v1/generate -d @payload.json```
payload.json uses a ~32k token prompt, and `max_tokens: 8192`, `stream: true`. after ~8s the runner memory spikes and container restarts.
2) env: g4dn-like GPU, quantized runtime v2.3.4, kernel optimizations OFF.

mike-eng: collected more logs from the crashed container: ```[2026-03-17T12:07:26Z] kv_cache: entries=1.2M size=27GB; trying alloc 6GB -> std::bad_alloc -> segfault```
emma-reliability: immediate short-term: 1) reduce allowed max_tokens for hosted default to 4096 for affected model variant, 2) enable prefetch backoff for long-context customers, 3) push a hotfix to runtime to guard against unbounded kv growth (quota on kv entries).
lia-support: CS updated customer about fallback routing; they want root cause and how to avoid this for Production. Also pushed billing hold pending investigation.
infra-oncall: next: collecting heap + nvprof from drained node repro; will attach to the ticket. also suggestion: 2-minute autoscaler cooldown + faster eviction to avoid repeated OOMKill flapping.
sanjay-ml: for reproduction we should test variations: smaller max_tokens, different quant flags, and model variant with attention_opt enabled. I'll run a matrix overnight and post results.
mike-eng: created a short-run runbook in the channel: steps to triage OOM vs segfault, pointer to `infra-oncall` drain playbook, and commands to repro. link: https://redwood.internal/playbooks/infer-oom-triage (internal).
emma-reliability: assigned to eng-runtime (mike-eng, sanjay-ml) to implement kv caps + safer attention kernel path. recommend rollback of v2.3.4->v2.3.3 for the fleet if we see >5% repeat on same node.
lia-support: Thanks. CS wants an estimated ETA for hotfix or rollback to communicate to customer. can we get an ETA in next 30m? :hourglass_flowing_sand: 
mike-eng: ETA for temporary config changes (reduce max_tokens + routing) is ~15m. Hotfix for runtime guard 2-4 hours. rollback can be started in 45m if needed. I'll update once confirmed.
alert-bot: [UPDATE] HealthMate's 504 rate dropped to 1.2% after fallback routing and max_tokens change.
lia-support: marking customer escalation open, ticket #CS-7234. will keep cs/cust updated.
emma-reliability: followups: - capture min repro package from customer - gather flamegraphs from crashed runs - decide rollback cutoff (if >3 nodes show same crash pattern). I'll schedule a quick sync in 20m.
mike-eng: noted, uploading crash artifacts to the incident folder now.```
